text:
Adam Fantilli ended it 59 seconds into overtime, a power-play slap shot that gave Columbus a 2-1 win over Vegas on a night when the Golden Knights had the better of the play. Fantilli, drafted third overall by the Blue Jackets in 2023, was named second star. The first star went to Cam Talbot, and that tells you who kept Columbus in it.

Talbot stopped 26 of 27 shots, and by our numbers Vegas created about 3.4 expected goals, meaning the quality of its chances added up to more than three goals' worth. Talbot saved roughly 2.4 goals more than those chances should have produced. Vegas won 68 percent of our simulated replays of every shot, against 32 percent for Columbus. Vegas was strongest in the third period, out-chancing the Blue Jackets 1.65 to 0.46 in expected goals. Braeden Bowman had the best look that missed, a 27 percent chance in that period that went off target.

The goals came early. Denton Mateychuk, the 12th pick in 2022, put Columbus ahead with a backhand at 11:51 of the first, and Tomas Hertl answered with a snap shot at 17:13 to make it 1-1. Nothing else got through until overtime, when the Blue Jackets drew their third power play of the night and cashed in on it. The facts we have for this game don't include standings or streaks for either club, so we'll leave it there: Columbus took two points it probably didn't earn on chances, and Vegas has a loss it didn't deserve.
